subject: On-prem KMS egress & bastion/proxy proposal for AtlasHealth
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@prisec.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AtlasHealth on-prem KMS integration & egress constraints

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this on. AtlasHealth has strict networking constraints for their private deployment and we need to validate Redwood's proposed KMS/HSM integration pattern against them before we proceed to PO. High-level constraints from their security team: 

- No direct outbound traffic to the public internet from the HSM/VPC subnets (customer allows only a set of managed egress targets via an internal NAT/proxy).
- Any attestation/CRL/OCSP calls must go via an approved relay inside the customer's VPC or through an approved partner connection (no arbitrary 3rd-party endpoints).
- All key import/export must be auditable; BYOK flow must include a tamper-evident attestation record and audit log ingestion into their SIEM.
- Key rotation windows: monthly for wrapping keys, quarterly for master KEKs; need a rollback plan for failed rotations.

Questions we need help with from Redwood:
1) Can you propose an architecture that keeps HSM traffic within the customer VPC (egress only to an allowlisted proxy) while still supporting Redwood-managed attestation?
2) What minimal set of egress ports/IPs will AtlasHealth need to allow?
3) What's the impact on inference latency if the KMS calls (unwrap/wrap) are proxied vs local HSM?

Attaching AtlasHealth's security requirements (atlas-security-reqs-07072027.pdf).

Can we set up a technical review later this week with your infra/security folks?

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of Security, PriSec
(on behalf of AtlasHealth)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@prisec.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, michael_grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasHealth on-prem KMS integration & egress constraints

Emily — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. I've started a short proposal and a rough network diagram (attached). High-level recommendation from our side:

- Deploy the HSM inside the AtlasHealth VPC (customer-managed HSM/NIC), with Redwood running a small attestation relay inside the same VPC via an approved partner VPC peering or PrivateLink. This keeps the HSM traffic on-private and avoids going out to the public internet.
- Where partner connectivity isn't available, use a narrow bastion/proxy pattern: a hardened egress proxy (customer-managed) which forwards only mTLS-attested PKCS#11 sessions to Redwood's attestation relay. The proxy will be allowlisted at Redwood by IP and present a client cert.
- BYOK flow: key material is generated customer-side inside the HSM and an attestation blob is exported to the proxy. Redwood ingests the attestation blob (via the relay) and records tamper-evident metadata into our immutable audit store.
- Rotation: support rolling KEK rotation via dual-wrap: new KEK pre-propagated to test path then cutover. If cutover fails, revert to prior KEK via documented rollback steps.

I'll attach the initial proposal text (proposal-egress-proxy.txt) and a network diagram (network-diagram-v0.drawio).

Next steps I propose: 1) a 60-minute technical sync Wed 7/21 to walk the diagram with Atlas and PriSec; 2) Michael to draft minimal firewall/NAT rules; 3) we prepare a short latency impact test plan (simple unwrapped token path vs proxied path).

If that works I'll coordinate calendars.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments

On Mon, Jul 19, 2027 at 11:03 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'll attach the initial proposal text and a network diagram.

Quick notes from product/security perspective:

- We need concrete SLO/latency targets for any path that touches the HSM during inference. If unwrap/wrap is on-path for generation, the customer needs to accept additional p50/p95. Please include expected token-level latency delta for both the Local-HSM (no proxy) and Proxy-Attestation patterns.
- KV cache placement is critical: recommend keeping KV cache and model-serving endpoints in the same VPC as the HSM for high-throughput workloads to avoid cross-VPC hops.
- For key rotation, document the exact window and the observable signals that indicate a safe rollback (e.g., error rates, latency spikes, failed unwrappings).

We should surface a brief compliance checklist for Atlas: attestations collected, audit stream to SIEM (format), and retention window. I'll own that artifact.

— Hannah

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-20T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasHealth on-prem KMS integration & egress constraints — firewall + proxy notes

I've sketched a concrete rule set and test knobs (see attached firewall-rule-set.csv). A few implementation details to consider:

- Ports: PKCS#11 typically over local sockets; our attestation relay will accept mTLS on TCP 443 (we can run on a nonstandard port if needed). For the proxy pattern, customer needs to allow outbound to Redwood relay IP(s) on that port only.
- Egress IPs: I'll provide a tight list of /32s for the relay during scoping; for now assume a small pool (3 IPs) that we can assign to the relay endpoints.
- NAT/proxy: prefer using a customer-managed NAT + egress proxy (Envoy with mTLS) that validates the HSM proxy certificate and forwards to Redwood. Do not permit plain HTTP or port forwarding.
- Private connectivity: If Atlas uses Transit Gateway or PrivateLink, we can host the attestation relay in our partner VPC and avoid public egress entirely — this is the recommended production pattern.
- Test vs Prod: recommend SoftHSM in an isolated test subnet for functional/latency tests. Production must use FIPS-validated HSM (vendor to be confirmed by Atlas).

Actionable ask for the sync: Atlas to confirm whether they can provision PrivateLink/Transit gateway peering or if we must design the hardened proxy option. Also need target latency SLOs to tune batching and cache timeouts.

— Michael
Michael Grant
Staff Infrastructure Engineer

Subject: Re: AtlasHealth on-prem KMS integration & egress constraints — Decisions & next steps

Emily / Atlas team — thanks for the quick turnaround and for joining the sync. Summary of decisions and next actions based on the review: 

1) Production pattern: PrivateLink (preferred) or Transit Gateway peering to host Redwood attestation relay inside Atlas's network. If Atlas can provision PrivateLink, no public egress will be required.
2) Fallback pattern: Hardened customer-managed egress proxy that performs mTLS to Redwood relay. Proxy must allow only PKCS#11 over mTLS and present a client cert; Redwood will provide allowlisted relay IPs and the server cert.
3) BYOK flow: customer generates keys within their HSM and sends an attestation blob to the relay; Redwood stores tamper-evident metadata and writes audit events to the agreed SIEM endpoint.
4) Rotation: we will support dual-wrap pre-propagation and an automated rollback window. Michael will produce a runbook with measurable signals for rollback.

Action items: 
- Atlas/PriSec: confirm whether PrivateLink/TransitGateway is available (owner: Atlas).
- Michael: share exact egress IPs and firewall CSV (owner: Michael) — due EOD 7/22.
- Hannah: draft compliance checklist and retention window (owner: Hannah) — due 7/23.
- Vivek: prepare latency test plan and schedule canary (owner: Vivek) — propose start 7/26.

I'll open a HubSpot deal activity and attach the approved artifacts (see links). If Atlas confirms PrivateLink we can move to scoping and a pilot next week.

Thanks all — good progress.

— Vivek
